full_text_en:
China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Urumqi Office v. Xinjiang Huadian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Hongyanchi Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd., et al. — dispute over loan contract

【Ruling Summary】

I. Registered capital is the most fundamental asset of a company. Determining and maintaining a certain amount of capital for a company is of significant value in establishing the company's basic debt repayment capacity and protecting the interests of creditors and the security of transactions. Capital contribution by shareholders is a basic requirement of the principle of capital determination and maintenance. Capital contribution is the most fundamental and important obligation of shareholders. Shareholders shall fully pay the amount of capital they have subscribed for as stipulated in the company's articles of association within the prescribed period. Where capital is contributed in monetary form, the full amount shall be deposited into the company's bank account. Where capital is contributed in non-monetary property, the transfer procedures for the property rights shall be completed in accordance with the law.

II. Pursuant to Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, the creation and transfer of property rights in movable property take effect upon delivery, and the transfer of ownership of movable property is based on actual delivery. Where a shareholder makes a capital contribution in the form of movable property as tangible assets, the movable property used as the capital contribution shall be actually delivered to the company within the prescribed period. If the property is not actually delivered, it shall be determined that the shareholder has not fulfilled its capital contribution obligation and that the capital contribution has not been actually made in place.

Civil Judgment of the Supreme People's Court

(2008) Min Er Zhong Zi No. 79

Appellant (Plaintiff at First Instance): China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Urumqi Office. Domicile: No. 19 Renmin Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Responsible Person: He Xiaochu, General Manager of this Office.

Agent ad litem: Huang Jiangdong, Staff Member of this Office.

Agent ad litem: Li Baojiang, Attorney at Tianyang (Beijing) Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Huadian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. Domicile: East Klamay Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Sun Gang, General Manager of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Liu Ruiping, Attorney at Xinjiang Zhongwang Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Huadian Hongyanchi Power Generation Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 3 Yan'an Er Village, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Sun Qingsong, General Manager of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Yuling, Attorney at Xinjiang Xinghe Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 618 Qidaowan South Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Zeng Qingfeng, Chairman of the Board of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Jiangzheng, Staff Member of this Company.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Huadian Hami Power Generation Co., Ltd. Domicile: Huoshiquan, Hami City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Zeng Qingfeng, Chairman of the Board of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Yuling, Attorney at Xinjiang Xinghe Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Huadian Kashi Power Generation Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 18 Century Avenue, Kashi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Zeng Qingfeng, Chairman of the Board of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Zhonghan, Attorney at Xinjiang Jin Cheng Xin Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Huadian Changji Thermal Power Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 55 South Oasis Road, Changji City, Changji Hui Autonomous Prefecture, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Li Dongzheng, Chairman of the Board of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Xu Zhonghan, Attorney at Xinjiang Jin Cheng Xin Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Urumqi Hongneng Property Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 3 Yan'an Er Village, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Xie Wenjin, General Manager of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Yang Yuling, Attorney at Xinjiang Xinghe Law Firm.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Jinma Property Management Co., Ltd. Domicile: No. 32 Qidaowan Road, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Sui Guofu, General Manager of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Jiangzheng, Staff Member of Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd.

Appellee (Defendant at First Instance): Xinjiang Weihuliang Power Plant Huayuan Electric Power Installation Company. Domicile: Xinjiang Weihuliang Power Plant, Urumqi City, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region.

Legal Representative: Zhou Fulin, General Manager of this Company.

Agent ad litem: Li Jiangzheng, Staff Member of Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd.

The Appellant, China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation, Urumqi Office (hereinafter referred to as Great Wall Urumqi Office), filed an appeal with this Court against the Civil Judgment (2007) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 25 rendered by the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region regarding the dispute over a loan contract with the Appellees, Xinjiang Huadian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Industry & Trade Company), Xinjiang Huadian Hongyanchi Power Generation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongyanchi Power Generation Company), Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Weihuliang Power Generation Company), Xinjiang Huadian Hami Power Generation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hami Power Generation Company), Xinjiang Huadian Kashi Power Generation Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Kashi Power Generation Company), Xinjiang Huadian Changji Thermal Power Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Changji Thermal Power Company), Urumqi Hongneng Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Hongneng Company), Xinjiang Jinma Property Management Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Jinma Company), and Xinjiang Weihuliang Power Plant Huayuan Electric Power Installation Company (hereinafter referred to as Installation Company). This Court formed a collegial panel in accordance with the law, with Adjudicator Qian Xiaochen serving as the Presiding Judge, and Acting Adjudicators Liu Min and Yang Zhengyu participating in the trial of this case. The court clerk Yuan Hongxia served as the record keeper. The trial of this case has now been concluded.

On June 21, 2007, Great Wall Urumqi Office filed a lawsuit with the High People's Court of Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region, requesting a judgment: 1. Ordering Industry & Trade Company to pay the loan principal of RMB 48,526,500 and interest of RMB 5,808,622. 2. Ordering Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, Changji Thermal Power Company, Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Installation Company to bear joint and several liability for repayment. 3. Ordering the Defendants at First Instance to bear the litigation costs.

The court of first instance found the following facts upon trial:

I. On August 17, 2004, Industry & Trade Company entered into the (2004) Bei Zi No. 0456 Working Capital Loan Contract with the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Urumqi Xinmin Road Sub-branch (hereinafter referred to as ICBC Xinmin Road Sub-branch), agreeing that ICBC Xinmin Road Sub-branch would provide a loan of RMB 50,000,000 to Industry & Trade Company, with a loan term from August 17, 2004 to August 16, 2005, an interest rate of 4.425 per thousand per month, and overdue interest calculated at 2.1 per ten thousand per day. On the same day, ICBC Xinmin Road Sub-branch provided the loan of RMB 50,000,000 to Industry & Trade Company pursuant to this Working Capital Loan Contract. On July 22, 2005, the Industrial and Commercial Bank of China, Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Branch, entered into the Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement (No. 3002000000115) with Great Wall Urumqi Office, transferring to Great Wall Urumqi Office the creditor's rights held by ICBC Xinmin Road Sub-branch against Industry & Trade Company under the (2004) Bei Zi No. 0456 Working Capital Loan Contract. On August 11, 2005, Great Wall Urumqi Office published a notice in Xinjiang Daily to Industry & Trade Company regarding the transfer of creditor's rights. After Great Wall Urumqi Office acquired the creditor's rights in this case, Industry & Trade Company repaid RMB 1,473,500 to Great Wall Urumqi Office. The interest on the loan in this case for the period from March 20, 2005 to May 27, 2005 amounted to RMB 7,508,803.

II. Industry & Trade Company was established on June 5, 2003, with a registered capital of RMB 10,000,000. Its promoter shareholders were Hongyanchi Power Generation Company (formerly known as Xinjiang Hongyanchi No. 2 Power Generation Co., Ltd.), Weihuliang Power Generation Company (formerly known as Xinjiang Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd.), Hami Power Generation Company (formerly known as Xinjiang Hami Tianguang Power Generation Co., Ltd.), Kashi Power Generation Company (formerly known as Xinjiang Kashi Power Generation Co., Ltd.), Changji Thermal Power Company (formerly known as Xinjiang Changji Thermal Power Co., Ltd.), Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Installation Company. Article 9 of the Articles of Association of Industry & Trade Company at the time of its establishment recorded the following capital contribution ratios and methods agreed upon by the promoter shareholders: Hongyanchi Power Generation Company was to contribute with warehouses and oil storage tanks valued at RMB 3,000,000; Weihuliang Power Generation Company was to contribute with warehouses and oil storage tanks valued at RMB 2,000,000; Hami Power Generation Company was to contribute with warehouses and oil storage tanks valued at RMB 1,500,000; Kashi Power Generation Company was to contribute with warehouses and oil storage tanks valued at RMB 1,500,000; Changji Thermal Power Company was to contribute with warehouses and oil storage tanks valued at RMB 1,500,000; Hongneng Company was to contribute with monetary capital of RMB 250,000; Jinma Company was to contribute with monetary capital of RMB 100,000; and Installation Company was to contribute with monetary capital of RMB 150,000. Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Installation Company all fully fulfilled their monetary capital contribution obligations to Industry & Trade Company in accordance with the agreement. After the establishment of Industry & Trade Company, the warehouses contributed as capital by Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company did not undergo ownership change procedures. On July 25, 2006, the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Administration for Industry and Commerce accordingly issued the Administrative Penalty Decision Xin Gong Shang Chu (2006) No. 21, ordering Industry & Trade Company to make up for the capital contributions. On August 6, 2006, the shareholders' meeting of Industry & Trade Company resolved that Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company would make up for the insufficient capital contributions in the form of machinery and equipment and replace the original equipment contributions. On September 20, 2006, Industry & Trade Company amended Article 9 of its Articles of Association at the time of establishment concerning the capital contribution methods of Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company, stipulating that Hongyanchi Power Generation Company would contribute with equipment valued at RMB 3,000,000, Weihuliang Power Generation Company with equipment valued at RMB 2,000,000, Hami Power Generation Company with equipment valued at RMB 1,500,000, Kashi Power Generation Company with equipment valued at RMB 1,500,000, and Changji Thermal Power Company with equipment valued at RMB 1,500,000. On September 28, 2006, Xinjiang Hongchang Certified Public Accountants Co., Ltd. issued the Capital Verification Report (2006) 8-074 regarding the shareholders' supplementary and replacement capital contributions, certifying that the supplementary and replacement capital contributions by Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company had all been made in place. Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company completed ownership transfer procedures with Industry & Trade Company for the machinery and equipment contributed as supplementary capital. The relevant documents for the supplementary capital contributions by Industry & Trade Company were all filed and registered with the administrative department for industry and commerce.

III. On June 18, 2007, Great Wall Urumqi Office filed an application for property preservation with the court of first instance, requesting the freezing, sealing up, or seizure of Industry & Trade Company's property. On June 22, 2007, the court issued the Civil Ruling (2007) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 25-1 pursuant to Great Wall Urumqi Office's property preservation application, ruling to freeze Industry & Trade Company's bank deposits, and if insufficient, to seal up or seize corresponding property. During the period from June 27, 2007 to July 3, 2007, the court, pursuant to the Civil Ruling (2007) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 25-1, sealed up the corresponding machinery and equipment contributed as supplementary capital by Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company.

The court of first instance found in its trial:

I. The (2004) Bei Zi No. 0456 Working Capital Loan Contract and the Creditor's Rights Transfer Agreement (No. 3002000000115) were the true expressions of the parties' intent, did not violate mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and should be confirmed as valid. After Great Wall Urumqi Office acquired the creditor's rights involved in this case, Industry & Trade Company had no objection. Therefore, Industry & Trade Company should repay the loan and pay interest to Great Wall Urumqi Office in accordance with the (2004) Bei Zi No. 0456 Working Capital Loan Contract. Industry & Trade Company had already repaid RMB 1,473,500, and the amount of loan still outstanding was RMB 48,526,500. Industry & Trade Company had no objection that the interest on the loan in this case for the period from March 20, 2005 to May 27, 2005 amounted to RMB 7,508,803. However, since Great Wall Urumqi Office only paid the case acceptance fee for the interest of RMB 5,808,622, the court of first instance did not try the portion of interest amounting to RMB 1,700,181 for which no case acceptance fee was paid, and Great Wall Urumqi Office could file a separate lawsuit. Therefore, Industry & Trade Company should repay the loan principal of RMB 48,526,500 and pay the interest of RMB 5,808,622 for the period from March 20, 2005 to May 27, 2005 to Great Wall Urumqi Office.

II. At the time of the establishment of Industry & Trade Company, the warehouses contributed as capital by Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company did not undergo ownership change procedures, which constituted insufficient capital contribution. However, the total amount of monetary and equipment capital contributions by the shareholders of Industry & Trade Company had reached the minimum amount required by the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, so Industry & Trade Company still had legal personality.

Article 1 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning How Financial Institutions Shall Assume Civil Liability for Issuing Untrue or False Capital Verification Reports or Fund Certificates for Enterprises (Fa (2002) No. 21) provides: "Where a contributor fails to make a capital contribution or fails to make a full capital contribution, but a financial institution provides an untrue or false capital verification report or fund certificate for the enterprise, and the relevant party, using such report or certificate, engages in economic dealings with the enterprise and suffers losses, the enterprise shall bear civil liability. Where the enterprise's property is insufficient to pay off its debts, the contributor shall be liable within the scope of the insufficient or false capital contribution." Article 4 of the same Notice provides: "Where a contributor fails to make a full capital contribution at the time of enterprise registration but later makes up for it, or where the contract on which the creditor's claim is based is invalid, the liability for compensation of the financial institution that conducted the capital verification shall be exempted." Article 10 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases Involving Civil Tort Compensation by Accounting Firms in Audit Business Activities (Fa Shi (2007) No. 12) provides: "Where a people's court determines, in accordance with Article 6 of these Provisions, that an accounting firm shall bear corresponding liability for compensation commensurate with its degree of fault, it shall handle the matter according to the following circumstances: (1) The audited entity shall first compensate the interested party for its losses. Where the contributor of the audited entity makes a false capital contribution, an untrue capital contribution, or withdraws capital contributions, and fails to make up for it afterwards, and after compulsory enforcement of the audited entity's property in accordance with the law, the losses are still not fully compensated, the contributor shall bear supplementary liability for compensation to the interested party within the scope of the false capital contribution, untrue capital contribution, or withdrawn capital contribution. (2) Where, after compulsory enforcement of the property of the audited entity and the contributor in accordance with the law, the losses are still not fully compensated, the accounting firm shall bear corresponding liability for compensation within the scope of the untrue audit amount. (3) The liability for compensation borne by an accounting firm to one or more interested parties shall be limited to the untrue audit amount." Pursuant to the above provisions, where a shareholder of a company fails to make a full capital contribution but the company still has legal personality, the shareholder shall only bear supplementary liability for compensation to the company's creditors within the scope of the insufficient capital contribution. If the shareholder makes up for the capital contribution, it shall not bear civil liability for the company's debts. Specifically in this case, first, where Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company did not make full capital contributions at the time of the establishment of Industry & Trade Company, and Industry & Trade Company had legal personality, these companies should only bear supplementary liability for compensation for Industry & Trade Company's debts within the scope of their insufficient capital contributions. Great Wall Urumqi Office's claim that they should bear joint and several liability for Industry & Trade Company's debts was unfounded. Second, after the establishment of Industry & Trade Company, Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company had resolved to make up for and replace their capital contributions, completed capital verification procedures for the supplementary and replacement capital contributions, completed ownership transfer procedures for the property used for supplementary and replacement capital contributions, and filed and registered the relevant documents for the supplementary and replacement capital contributions with the administrative department for industry and commerce. These actions complied with legal provisions and should be deemed as having made up for their capital contributions, with all capital contributions fully made in place. Since Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashi Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company had already made up for their capital contributions, with all contributions fully in place, they should no longer bear civil liability for Industry & Trade Company's debts. Therefore, Great Wall Urumqi Office's claim that they should bear civil liability for Industry & Trade Company's debts was unfounded.

III. Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Anzhuang Company each fully performed their monetary capital contribution obligations to Industry and Trade Company in accordance with the agreement. The reason asserted by the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall was unfounded. Article 28 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, effective before January 1, 2006, provided: "After the establishment of a limited liability company, if it is discovered that the actual value of the in-kind contributions, industrial property rights, non-patented technology, or land use rights contributed as capital is significantly lower than the amount stipulated in the company's articles of association, the shareholder who made such contribution shall make up the difference, and the other shareholders at the time of the company's establishment shall bear joint and several liability." Article 31 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, effective from January 1, 2006, provides: "After the establishment of a limited liability company, if it is discovered that the actual value of the non-monetary property contributed as capital for the establishment of the company is significantly lower than the amount stipulated in the company's articles of association, the shareholder who made such contribution shall make up the difference; the other shareholders at the time of the company's establishment shall bear joint and several liability." According to the above provisions, when the actual value of the non-monetary property contributed by the company's founding shareholders for the establishment of the company is significantly lower than the amount stipulated in the company's articles of association, the shareholder who made such contribution is obligated to make up the difference, and the other shareholders at the time of the company's establishment shall bear joint and several liability for the corresponding civil liability of the shareholder obligated to make up the difference. However, the above provisions only apply to situations where the actual value of the non-monetary capital contributions of the company's shareholders is significantly lower than the amount stipulated in the company's articles of association, and not to other situations. The Urumqi Office of the Great Wall did not assert that there existed a situation where the actual value of the non-monetary capital contributions of Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company was significantly lower than the amount stipulated in the company's articles of association. Yet at trial, it requested Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Anzhuang Company to bear joint and several liability for the insufficient capital contributions of Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company under Article 31 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China effective from January 1, 2006. Its reasoning was untenable. In summary, in accordance with Article 80, Articles 205 and 206 of the Contract Law of the People's Republic of China, and Article 10 of the Supreme People's Court's Several Provisions on Issues Concerning Civil Tort Compensation Involving Accounting Firms in Audit Business Activities, the court hereby ruled: 1. Industry and Trade Company shall, within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment, repay the loan principal of RMB 48,526,500 to the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall; 2. Industry and Trade Company shall, within 15 days from the effective date of the judgment, pay interest of RMB 5,808,622 for the period from March 20, 2005 to May 27, 2005 to the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall; 3. The other claims of the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall are dismissed. The case acceptance fee of RMB 313,475.62 and the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Industry and Trade Company.

The Urumqi Office of the Great Wall, dissatisfied with the above civil judgment of the original trial court, filed an appeal with this court, asserting: I. The original trial judgment failed to respond to the application made by the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall, violating procedural law. II. The original trial judgment improperly admitted copies of documentary evidence provided by Industry and Trade Company. The capital verification report issued by Xinjiang Hongchang Limited Liability Accounting Firm and the written materials regarding the transfer of machinery and equipment contributed as capital by the shareholders of Industry and Trade Company to Industry and Trade Company, as provided by Industry and Trade Company, were all copies. The original trial judgment, relying solely on these copies, found that the shareholders of Industry and Trade Company had fully paid their capital contributions, violating the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Several Rules on Evidence in Civil Proceedings. III. The original trial judgment erred in its findings of fact. When the original trial court served the notice of assistance in execution on the appellees in this case, the investigation conducted on the appellees was facts confirmed by the court. The records and photographs taken confirmed that the shareholders of Industry and Trade Company made false capital contributions, that the replaced contributed property had never been delivered, and that it had been possessed and used by each shareholder from beginning to end. Moreover, based on the nature of the property intended to be contributed, these mechanical devices were property that could not be transferred and could never have been transferred to Industry and Trade Company. In summary, the appellant requested the court of second instance to rule: 1. Set aside the Civil Judgment (2007) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 25. 2. The appellees, Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, Changji Thermal Power Company, Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Anzhuang Company, shall bear joint and several liability for repayment in this case. 3. The litigation costs shall be borne by the appellees.

In response to the appeal requests and reasons of the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall, Industry and Trade Company argued in its defense: I. The facts and repayment liability claimed by the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall are unrelated to the shareholders of Industry and Trade Company. The liability for Industry and Trade Company's borrowing from the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall shall be independently borne by Industry and Trade Company as a civil liability. II. All registered capital of Industry and Trade Company's shareholders was paid in full in accordance with the law: (a) The actions of Industry and Trade Company's shareholders throughout the process of company establishment, capital verification, and shareholder qualification all complied with legal provisions and were confirmed as valid by the relevant authorities. (b) When Industry and Trade Company was established, the ownership of the warehouse property contributed by some shareholders was not transferred. The Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region Administration for Industry and Commerce issued a penalty decision ordering the replenishment of capital contributions. Those shareholders, with the approval of the Administration for Industry and Commerce, replaced these with in-kind assets. The above actions complied with legal provisions. (c) The Urumqi Office of the Great Wall is actually challenging the administrative actions of the competent authority of the Administration for Industry and Commerce in lawfully reviewing and approving the establishment and capital verification procedures of the defendant. Such challenges are not to be resolved through civil procedure. (d) The Urumqi Office of the Great Wall seeks to overturn the capital verification reports of Industry and Trade Company and its shareholders, which were confirmed by the statutory capital verification authority, and the registration procedures reviewed and approved by the administrative department for industry and commerce, while confusing shareholder rights and interests with the ownership, use, and operation rights of company property. (e) The evidence at trial proves that the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall's naming of Industry and Trade Company's shareholders as defendants constitutes an unjustified action. In summary, the original trial judgment had clear findings of fact and correctly applied the law. The appellee requested that the court of second instance dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

In response to the appeal requests and reasons of the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall, Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, Changji Thermal Power Company, Jinma Company, and Anzhuang Company each argued in their defense: I. Industry and Trade Company meets the conditions of a legal person and shall independently bear liability in accordance with the law. II. The trial procedure of the original trial court was lawful. III. The capital verification report submitted by Industry and Trade Company to the court originated from the Urumqi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce and was affixed with the official seal of the Urumqi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, giving it legal evidentiary effect. In summary, the appellees requested that the court of second instance dismiss the appeal and uphold the original judgment.

In response to the appeal requests and reasons of the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall, Hami Power Generation Company and Hongneng Company argued in their defense: I. Industry and Trade Company meets the conditions of a legal person and shall independently bear liability in accordance with the law. II. The trial procedure of the original trial court was lawful. III. The capital verification report submitted by Industry and Trade Company to the court originated from the Urumqi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce and was affixed with the official seal of the Urumqi Municipal Administration for Industry and Commerce, giving it legal evidentiary effect. IV. In September 2006, when some shareholders of Industry and Trade Company replenished their capital contributions, the assets provided met the requirements of Article 27 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China. They were not assets that could not be transferred. These assets were appraised and verified by an accounting firm and were reviewed, approved, and filed by the industry and commerce department, fully complying with legal provisions for capital contribution assets. According to the provisions of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, where a shareholder fails to make timely capital contributions, the shareholder is obligated to make up the contributions. Since some shareholders have made up their contributions, they are no longer required to bear liability for the debts arising from the operation of Industry and Trade Company within the scope of their capital contributions. In summary, the appellees requested that the court of second instance, in accordance with the law, dismiss the appellant's appeal and uphold the original judgment.

In the second instance, this court confirms the findings of fact by the original trial court, except for the portion concerning Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company having completed their capital contribution obligations to Industry and Trade Company. Additionally, it is found that: As of the time of the filing of this case, Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company had not actually delivered the relevant equipment such as oil storage tanks and oil supply pumps to Industry and Trade Company in accordance with the resolutions of the shareholders' meeting of Industry and Trade Company on August 6, 2006, and the provisions of the newly amended articles of association of Industry and Trade Company on September 20, 2006. The above-mentioned equipment intended for capital contribution was still possessed and used by Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company, respectively.

This court holds that the loan contract involved in this case is a true expression of the parties' intentions, does not violate the mandatory provisions of laws or administrative regulations, and shall be valid. After the loan under this contract matured, Industry and Trade Company failed to repay in full and shall, in accordance with the law, repay the borrowing and pay interest to the creditor, the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall. The parties have no objection to the above content of the original trial judgment, and this court upholds it.

The main issues in dispute in the second instance are whether the shareholders of Industry and Trade Company have fully paid their capital contributions and whether they should bear civil liability for the debts of Industry and Trade Company in this case.

The capital contributions of the shareholders of Industry and Trade Company are divided into two parts: monetary contributions and in-kind contributions. Regarding the monetary contributions, during the establishment of Industry and Trade Company, Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Anzhuang Company paid monetary capital contributions to Industry and Trade Company in the amounts of RMB 250,000, RMB 100,000, and RMB 150,000, respectively. There is no factual evidence to support the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall's claim that Hongneng Company, Jinma Company, and Anzhuang Company withdrew their capital contributions. This court does not uphold that claim. Industry and Trade Company received the above monetary capital contributions, which met the minimum registered capital requirement for enterprise legal persons stipulated in the Company Law, satisfying the basic conditions for the establishment of an enterprise legal person. It legally possesses an independent enterprise legal person status. The Urumqi Office of the Great Wall's claim that Industry and Trade Company does not have legal person status and that the shareholders should bear joint and several liability for the debts of Industry and Trade Company lacks factual and legal basis, and this court does not uphold it.

Regarding the in-kind capital contributions, during the establishment of Industry and Trade Company, the warehouses contributed as capital by Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company had not undergone ownership transfer procedures, constituting insufficient capital contribution. Subsequently, with the approval of the shareholders' meeting of Industry and Trade Company, the above shareholders undertook to replace the real property with their respective oil storage tanks, oil supply pumps, and related equipment as new in-kind capital contributions. However, as of the time of the filing of this case, the above equipment had not been actually delivered to Industry and Trade Company. It was still possessed and used by the shareholder companies. The documentation of in-kind delivery provided by Industry and Trade Company did not reflect the true situation of this case. The above equipment is chattel. According to Article 23 of the Property Law of the People's Republic of China, the creation and transfer of property rights in chattel take effect upon delivery. The transfer of ownership of chattel is based on actual delivery. Since the related equipment that the above shareholders promised to contribute as capital was not actually delivered to Industry and Trade Company, it shall be determined that the above shareholders failed to actually fulfill their promises of in-kind capital contributions, and the relevant capital contributions were not actually made in full. The Capital Verification Report (2006) No. 8-074 issued by Xinjiang Hongchang Limited Liability Accounting Firm and the relevant industrial and commercial registration filing materials for Industry and Trade Company's replenishment of capital contributions failed to reflect the true status of capital contributions. This court does not accept them.

Registered capital is the most fundamental asset of a company. Determining and maintaining a certain amount of capital in the company is of significant value for establishing the company's basic debt repayment capacity and protecting the interests of creditors and transaction security. Shareholder capital contributions are the basic requirement of the principle of capital determination and maintenance. Capital contribution is the most fundamental and important obligation of a company's shareholder, and it is also a legal obligation that the Company Law requires shareholders to undertake. According to Articles 28, paragraph 1, and Article 31 of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China, shareholders shall, in a timely manner and in full, pay the amounts of capital contributions they have subscribed for as stipulated in the company's articles of association. Where shareholders contribute capital in monetary form, they shall deposit the full amount of the monetary capital contribution into the bank account opened by the limited liability company; where they contribute capital in non-monetary property, they shall, in accordance with the law, go through the procedures for the transfer of the property rights thereof. After the establishment of a limited liability company, if it is discovered that the actual value of the non-monetary property contributed as capital for the establishment of the company is significantly lower than the amount stipulated in the company's articles of association, the shareholder who made such contribution shall make up the difference. Where a shareholder makes a false capital contribution, and the company's existing assets are insufficient to repay the debts of its creditors, the company's shareholder shall bear supplementary liability for compensation to the creditors within the scope of the false capital contribution amount. By reference to the relevant provisions of the Supreme People's Court's Reply on Issues Concerning Civil Liability After an Enterprise Established by an Enterprise is Revoked or Ceases Business, the Several Provisions on Issues Concerning the People's Court's Enforcement Work, and the Notice on How to Bear Civil Liability Where Financial Institutions Issue False or Fraudulent Capital Verification Reports or Capital Certificates for Enterprises, where an investor fails to make a capital contribution or fails to make a sufficient capital contribution, and the enterprise's property is insufficient to pay off its debts, the investor shall bear liability within the scope of the false or insufficient capital contribution amount. Hongyanchi Power Generation Company, Weihuliang Power Generation Company, Hami Power Generation Company, Kashgar Power Generation Company, and Changji Thermal Power Company shall each bear supplementary liability for compensation for the debts of Industry and Trade Company in this case within the scope of their respective insufficient capital contributions. The original trial judgment's finding that the above shareholders had completed their capital contribution obligations and its dismissal of the Urumqi Office of the Great Wall's claims were improper and should be reversed.

In summary, the original trial judgment had unclear factual findings and improperly applied the law. In accordance with Article 153, paragraph 1, items (1) and (3) of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, this court hereby rules as follows:

I. Affirm items 1 and 2 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2007) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 25 of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region;

II. Set aside item 3 of the main text of the Civil Judgment (2007) Xin Min Er Chu Zi No. 25 of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region;

III. If the property of Xinjiang Huadian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. is insufficient to satisfy the contents of item 1 of this judgment, then Xinjiang Huadian Hongyanchi Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Hami Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Kashgar Power Generation Co., Ltd., and Xinjiang Huadian Changji Thermal Power Co., Ltd. shall bear supplementary liability for compensation to the Urumqi Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation within the amounts of RMB 3,000,000, RMB 2,000,000, RMB 1,500,000, RMB 1,500,000, and RMB 1,500,000, respectively;

IV. Dismiss the other claims of the Urumqi Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation.

The first-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 313,475.62 shall be borne by Xinjiang Huadian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 263,475.62, and by Xinjiang Huadian Hongyanchi Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Hami Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Kashgar Power Generation Co., Ltd., and Xinjiang Huadian Changji Thermal Power Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 10,000 each; the property preservation fee of RMB 5,000 shall be borne by Xinjiang Huadian Industry & Trade Co., Ltd. The second-instance case acceptance fee of RMB 313,475.62 shall be borne by the Urumqi Office of China Great Wall Asset Management Corporation in the amount of RMB 263,475.62 (RMB 156,737.81 has been prepaid, and an additional RMB 106,737.81 must be paid), and by Xinjiang Huadian Hongyanchi Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Weihuliang Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Hami Power Generation Co., Ltd., Xinjiang Huadian Kashgar Power Generation Co., Ltd., and Xinjiang Huadian Changji Thermal Power Co., Ltd. in the amount of RMB 10,000 each.

This judgment is final.
